title: Edge Activation Lab Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a practical runbook for running a customer-facing Proof-of-Concept (POC) focused on edge / private deployments of Redwood Private. Target: deliver a working edge inference integration (VPC or on-prem edge gateway) with measurable latency/throughput baselines and a clear handoff to the customer SRE or our Dedicated ops team.

Scope:
- One-week technical activation lab with the customer (4 delivery days + buffer)
- Validate model serving (hosted on private nodes), KMS integration for keys, and network egress policies
- Measure p50/p95 latency for typical prompt sizes and estimated token throughput
- Produce a short runbook and rollback plan for production handoff

Audience:
Solutions engineers, customer SREs, customer infra, sales engineering, product PM for Private.

High-level objectives (must):
- End-to-end inference flow working inside customer VPC (request -> token auth -> model -> response)
- KMS access test and CMEK key rotation demo
- Observe latency under synthetic traffic (baseline: p95 < 450ms for small prompts on rtx-5000-class node)
- Validate autoscaling trigger (queue depth-based) and graceful fallback to smaller model under constrained capacity

Success criteria (POC acceptance):
- Customer can make authenticated calls via their network policy and see expected outputs
- Latency/throughput report with raw traces and token-level cost estimate
- Completed 1-week knowledge transfer session + runbook handed off to customer ops

Timeline & Sprint plan (one-week activation)
Day 0 (prep, internal):
- Confirm infra quotas, pre-provision test VMs (Ben)
- Share environment checklist with customer (Priya)
- Create JIRA board and ticket skeleton (SE-1789)

Day 1 (kickoff + baseline):
Morning: Kickoff w/ customer (intro, scope, risks, communications)
Afternoon: Network connectivity test (VPN / VPC peering), firewall rules, load balancer config
Owners: Miguel (network), Priya (customer comms)
Deliverable: connectivity-ok indicator, SSH + API reachability

Day 2 (model onboarding):
- Deploy model artifact (quantized variant) to edge node; run basic inference tests
- Validate KV cache warmup and streaming response path
Owners: Aisha (deploy), Ben (runtime tuning)
Deliverable: sample inference results and perf counters

Day 3 (security & keys):
- Integrate KMS/HSM (customer key) and run rotation test
- Audit log sampling and agent-side telemetry validation
Owners: Priya + customer infra lead
Deliverable: rotation_ok + audit-logs excerpt

Day 4 (load + observability):
- Synthetic load ramp: 0 -> target qps; measure p50/p95, GPU utilization, token/sec; record traces
- Run failure scenarios: node OOM, network flaps, model fallback to smaller variant
Owners: Miguel + Aisha
Deliverable: perf-report PDF + annotated flamegraph snippet

Day 5 (handoff & retro):
- Runbook walkthrough, open items, sign-off discussion, next steps for Dedicated handoff or extended pilot
- Finalize artifact bundle (runbook, scripts, perf logs) and put into Confluence space

Tasks & Owners (short form):
- Pre-provision edge nodes (Ben) — task: edge-provision-001 — due Day -1
- Prepare test dataset (customer + synthetic) (Priya) — due Day 0
- Create temp ingress rule for test API (Miguel) — due Day 1 AM
- Deploy model and sanity-check prompts (Aisha) — due Day 2 AM
- Instrument tracing and metrics (Ben) — due Day 2 PM
- KMS integration smoke (Priya) — due Day 3 AM
- Autoscale policy smoke and fallback test (Aisha) — due Day 4 AM
- Collect logs & package artifacts (Miguel) — due Day 4 PM

Acceptance tasks (concrete):
- curl + auth token to /v1/generate returns 200 and expected schema (owner: customer + Aisha)
- KMS key rotation invoked and new key used for next calls (owner: Priya)
- Synthetic load p95 < 450ms for small prompt (owner: Ben) or documented explanation if tradeoff

Playbook run checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm VPC CIDR and allowed IPs
- [ ] Confirm NAT/egress rules for telemetry upload
- [ ] Customer KMS credential handed via secure channel
- [ ] Model artifact checksum verified
- [ ] Monitoring dashboard pre-configured with token-level metrics

Runbook snippets (ops commands & notes):
- Deploy model: ./deploy_edge.sh --model my-model-v3 --quantize int8 --node edge-01 --region us-west-2
- Start trace collector: kubectl exec -n redwood trace-collector -- ./start --endpoint http://localhost:4317
- Simulate load: locust -f load/edge_ramp.py --users 100 --spawn-rate 20 --run-time 10m
Notes: watch KV cache hit-rate after warmup — first 200 requests will be higher latency.

Failure scenarios & rollback:
- If node OOM consistently on baseline traffic: reduce batch size and enable model fallback to smaller-family. Communicate to customer and schedule Dedicated-reserve talk.
- If KMS integration blocks: switch to temporary managed key (with customer sign-off) and continue tests; this is a security gating item — do not proceed to handoff without root-cause and mitigation plan.

Observed risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: Customer network ACLs introduce asymmetric routing causing packet drops. Mitigation: require test that demonstrates bi-directional TCP, provide packet-capture instructions.
- Risk: On-prem hardware slower than expected. Mitigation: run quick quantization-retry and propose edge pooling to aggregate capacity.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Does the customer expect SSO integration in week 1? (ask sales)
- Confirm which models are allowed under customer policy (list of approved OSS weights)
- Need a short legality blurb for audit logs and PII redaction — loop in legal if dataset has customer PII

Artifacts to deliver at the end of POC:
- Runbook (this doc trimmed + ops scripts)
- Performance report (p50/p95, GPU util, token/sec, cost estimate)
- Hand-off checklist and contact matrix
- Short recording of runbook walkthrough session (upload link in Confluence)

Meeting notes (Kickoff, Day 1):
- Customer: Acme Edge (primary contacts: Elias Rivera (infra), Jana Wu (security))
- Agreed guardrails: no external model downloads; only vetted models in allowed bucket
- Action: customer to open firewall rule to account IPs (Elias) — target: Day 1 afternoon

Next steps (immediate):
- Ben: finalize node images and attach test dataset — due in 24h
- Priya: send calendar invite + pre-kickoff checklist to customer 
- Aisha: confirm model artifact location and pre-signed URL to customer

Appendix (quick links & snippets):
- Debugging tips: capture /var/log/redwood/runtime.log and export with gzip; watch for repeated "cache miss" lines
- Helpful command: redwoodctl diag --node edge-01 --since 10m > diag-edge-01.json

-- END --
